nodes.summary: The exact hitting set problem is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to an exact-hitting-set instance that is both well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The exact HITTING SET decision problem

nodes.summary: An exact-hitting-set instance $(r, U)$ is feasible when there is a finite set $W$ of elements less than $r$ such that every listed subset $U_i$ contains exactly one element of $W$, that is $|W \cap U_i| = 1$ for each $i$ (counted with multiplicity in the list, which for well-formed instances is the size of the intersection).
nodes.title: Feasible exact-hitting-set instances

nodes.summary: An instance of the exact hitting set problem is a pair $(r, U)$: the number $r$ of elements $0, \dots, r-1$ and a finite list $U = (U_1, \dots, U_m)$ of finite lists of natural numbers, the subsets to be hit.
nodes.title: An exact-hitting-set instance

nodes.summary: The exact hitting set decision problem lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it. Recorded as wanted.
nodes.title: Karp's HITTING SET is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An exact-hitting-set instance $(r, U)$ is well formed when every list $U_i$ has no repeated entry and only entries less than $r$.
nodes.title: Well-formed exact-hitting-set instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
